markers.name: Iris-based mm calibration (infrastructure)
markers.definition: Converts pixels to mm using the visible iris (corneal) diameter as a known length
markers.formula: mm_per_px = D_ref / iris_px (mean of both eyes)
markers.ethnicNorms: Pooled adult corneal diameter 11.84 ± 0.79 mm (296,887 eyes, 234 studies). Iranian deep-learning HVID scaling: MAPE 2.8–4.8% (n not restated here). Arab: not found
markers.perception: n/a (enabler for all mm norms)

markers.name: Upper facial third proportion
markers.definition: Forehead height as a share of total face height
markers.landmarks: tr, g, me; tr: none (10 is not trichion), g≈9, me≈152
markers.ethnicNorms: Saudi tr-n basis: 35.2 % M, 36.6 % F (RoM, n = 168). tr-n > n-sn in 81.7 % M / 88 % F
markers.perception: Attractive female celebrities had more uniformly divided thirds than males [R15]. Milutinovic 2014 (cited in R43): uniform thirds/fifths in pleasing faces

markers.name: Middle facial third proportion
markers.definition: Glabella–subnasale as a share of face height
markers.perception: Sexually dimorphic in celebrities (F > M, p = .015) [R15]

markers.name: Lower facial third proportion
markers.definition: Subnasale–menton as a share of face height
markers.ethnicNorms: Saudi 35.4 % M / 33.7 % F (RoM, tr-n/n-sn/sn-gn basis). Lower third > middle third in 91.4 % of Saudi men and 88 % of women
markers.perception: Strongly dimorphic in attractive faces (M > F, p < .0001) [R15]

markers.name: Middle : lower third ratio (existing: midToLowerThird)
markers.definition: Nose height relative to lower-face height; works without the hairline
markers.landmarks: n or g, sn, me; 168 or 9, 2, 152
markers.normFemale: Saudi 3D 0.97 ± 0.13 (44); Saudi caliper 0.88 (RoM); NAW 0.79 (RoM); Egyptian women g-sn 45.53 ± 1.76 % vs sn-gn 54.34 ± 1.96 % of g-gn
markers.ethnicNorms: Farkas 2005 via R2: Egyptian 0.85 M / 0.82 F; Chinese 0.74 / 0.78; Turkish 0.88 / 0.93; African-American 0.66 / 0.68 (all RoM)
markers.perception: Not found as an attractiveness predictor in accessed sources

markers.name: Morphological facial index
markers.definition: Face height (nasion–menton) relative to bizygomatic width
markers.ethnicNorms: Persian F (n-me not given): not found. Croatian vs Syrian: index differed significantly (cited in R47, no values)
markers.perception: Not found

markers.name: Physiognomic face height / width
markers.definition: Trichion–menton relative to bizygomatic width
markers.perception: Pseudo-golden-ratio (1.618) thresholds are used by R3 but have no perceptual validation; Holland: phi mask fits masculinised fashion-model faces [R42]

markers.name: Facial width-to-height ratio (existing: fWHR)
markers.definition: Bizygomatic width over upper-face height (brow to upper lip)
markers.perception: Predicted reactive aggression in men (15 % of variance) and penalty minutes in hockey players (r = 0.54) [R31]

markers.name: Horizontal fifths
markers.definition: Five horizontal segments (outer face–ex, eye, intercanthal, eye, ex–outer face) as % of face width
markers.ethnicNorms: Arabian Saudi: not reported as fifths
markers.perception: Uniform fifths in pleasing faces (Milutinovic, cited in R43)
markers.automatable: auto-ratio (face edge at eye level ≈ contour)

markers.name: Bitemporal / bizygomatic ratio (existing: foreheadToFaceWidth)
markers.definition: Forehead (frontotemporale) width relative to face width
markers.ethnicNorms: Persian F min. frontal breadth 87.2 / zy 134.2 = 0.65 (RoM; ft defined differently)
markers.perception: Middle-East consensus: temple fullness preferred, especially under head covering [R7]

markers.name: Eye–mouth vertical distance / face length (Pallett ratio)
markers.definition: Vertical distance from the eye line to the mouth relative to face length (hairline–chin)
markers.perception: Attractiveness was optimised when the vertical eye–mouth distance was ≈36 % of face length; this matches an average face [R30] (abstract; exact landmark definitions not verified)
markers.automatable: review (hairline); auto-ratio if face length = n-me variant (unvalidated)

markers.name: Interpupillary / face width (Pallett ratio)
markers.definition: Distance between the eyes relative to face width
markers.perception: Attractiveness was optimised at ≈46 % of face width [R30]

markers.name: Eye–mouth–eye angle
markers.definition: Angle at the mouth centre between lines to both pupil centres
markers.perception: Highly sexually dimorphic and size-independent; male attractiveness correlated negatively with EME angle and with its asymmetry [R32]

markers.name: Vertical eye-level asymmetry
markers.definition: Difference in height of the pupils (and of the canthi) relative to the facial midline perpendicular
markers.normMale: Korean (mixed sex, n = 76): pupils 1.57 ± 1.10 mm; medial canthi 1.14 ± 1.07; lateral canthi 2.03 ± 1.64
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Bilateral landmark symmetry (existing: symmetry)
markers.definition: Mean mirrored-landmark deviation about the midline
markers.normMale: 3D: women more symmetrical than men; asymmetry rises with age (no single norm)
markers.perception: Mixed evidence: Kaipainen 2016 and Farrera 2015 (cited in R43) found no link between asymmetry and attractiveness; Komori 2009 found symmetry positive for both sexes

markers.name: Palpebral fissure length (eye width)
markers.definition: Endocanthion to exocanthion
markers.ethnicNorms: Saudi (Bokhari 2011) 30.8/29.5; Farkas 2005: Egyptian 31.5/30.8, Turkish 30.6/29.8, Chinese 29.4/28.5, African-American 32.9/32.4, Iranian 37.2/24.4 (implausible); Kenyan 34.0/33.7; HK Chinese 27.6/26.0; 3D Caucasian 31.15/29.69, Chinese 30.24/28.63. Ratio en-ex/zy-zy Egyptian F 0.254 (RoM). Pooled 2D PFL 29.2 ± 2.7 M / 28.1 ± 2.8 F
markers.perception: Rhee: attractive Caucasian/African composites have narrower fissure width and height than average ones; attractive Korean eyes are larger [R28]

markers.name: Palpebral fissure height
markers.definition: Palpebrale superius to inferius at mid-pupil
markers.ethnicNorms: HK Chinese 11.55/11.94; Malaysian South Indian 11.06/11.48 (n = 300). Arab: not found
markers.perception: Rhee [R28] (see above)

markers.name: Palpebral fissure index (existing: eyeAspect)
markers.definition: Height / length of the eye opening
markers.ethnicNorms: HK Chinese ×100: 41.8–43.1 M, 45.9 F. Arab: not found
markers.perception: "Frame concept": narrower eye-fissure frame rated more attractive (Benslimane 2017, cited in R43). ME consensus prefers large, almond-shaped eyes [R7]

markers.name: Canthal tilt (existing: canthalTilt)
markers.definition: Angle of the en→ex line above the horizontal (head-roll corrected)
markers.ethnicNorms: Black South African F 6.8° ± 2.7° (156); Malaysian South Indian 4.72° M / 7.04° F (300); Korean patients 8.45° ± 3.53° (76). Arab: not found. Definitions differ (true horizontal vs inter-endocanthion line)
markers.perception: Attractive females have greater tilt than attractive males [R15]. Rhee: attractive Asian composites less steep than average Asian; attractive Caucasian/African steeper than average [R28]

markers.name: Intercanthal width
markers.definition: Endocanthion to endocanthion
markers.ethnicNorms: Al-Qattan: in Saudis, men have a *smaller* en-en than women (reverse of other races); Saudi women wider than whites. Farkas 2005: Egyptian 31.8/30.9, Turkish 32.8/31.7, Chinese 37.9/36.5, African-American 35.8/34.4; HK 40.6/38.3; Kenyan 32.2/32.1
markers.perception: Regardless of race, attractive composites had wide-set eyes [R28]

markers.name: Intercanthal / eye width (existing: eyeSpacingRatio)
markers.definition: Eye spacing relative to eye width
markers.ethnicNorms: Saudi: ex-en > en-en in 55.9 % M / 74.7 % F; equal (±1 mm) in 29 % / 25 %. Kenyan: equal in 33 % / 27 %
markers.perception: Wide-set eyes in attractive composites [R28]. The "ideal = 1" target is not a population norm (Farkas 1985 [R41])

markers.name: Canthal index
markers.definition: Intercanthal width as a share of biocular width
markers.perception: Not found directly (see wide-set eyes, R28)

markers.name: Interpupillary distance
markers.definition: Pupil centre to pupil centre
markers.perception: Beautiful women and "femmes fatales" had the same IPD (Hwang 2015, cited in R43); no sex difference in attractive celebrities [R15]

markers.name: Biocular / bizygomatic width
markers.definition: Outer-canthal width relative to face width
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Upper-lid position (MRD1 proxy)
markers.definition: Pupil centre to upper lid margin
markers.formula: mm via iris scale; or ÷ iris diameter
markers.perception: Female celebrities had higher lids than males (p = .002); thyroid-eye-disease lids after surgery 4.8 mm were outside the "beautiful" mean [R22]
markers.automatable: auto-mm (uses iris centre, not corneal light reflex)

markers.name: Tarsal platform show (upper-lid exposure)
markers.definition: Visible pretarsal skin between upper lid margin and crease/fold at mid-pupil
markers.landmarks: lid margin, lid fold (not in MediaPipe)
markers.normMale: celebrity 2.50 ± 1.83 mm; 3D fold–margin distance Caucasian 3.35 ± 1.23, Chinese 1.54 ± 0.43
markers.ethnicNorms: Arab: not found. ME consensus: a "wide upper lid margin area" that emphasises the eye is desirable [R7]
markers.perception: Female celebrities show more TPS than males [R22]
markers.automatable: review / custom segmentation (crease not a mesh point)

markers.name: Brow fat span
markers.definition: Lid crease/fold to the lower edge of the brow at mid-pupil
markers.perception: n.s. by sex in celebrities [R22]

markers.name: TPS : BFS ratio
markers.definition: Upper-lid show relative to brow fat span (scale-free)
markers.perception: Larger ratio in female celebrities (p = .004): "more TPS and less BFS may be desirable for optimal female appearance" [R22]

markers.name: Inferior scleral show
markers.definition: Visible sclera between inferior limbus and lower lid margin
markers.perception: No attractive celebrity showed scleral show [R15]. Overall scleral exposure (not specifically inferior show) increased trust and attractiveness ratings in an experiment (162 raters, 50 faces) [R38]

markers.name: Iris width / eye width ("white show" horizontally)
markers.definition: Share of the eye opening occupied by the iris
markers.perception: Attractive Korean composites show "a lot of exposure of white in the medial and lateral area" [R28]

markers.name: Lateral / medial canthal angle (eye shape)
markers.definition: Opening angle at the lateral canthus relative to the medial canthus
markers.perception: Attractive Caucasian/African composites have a "keen, jaguar-like" eye shape [R28]. ME consensus: almond shape preferred [R7]

markers.name: Epicanthal fold presence
markers.definition: Fold covering the medial canthus
markers.ethnicNorms: Chinese medial canthal angle is larger, attributed to the epicanthus [R16]
markers.perception: Attractive Korean/Asian composites have no epicanthus [R28]

markers.name: Brow height at mid-pupil (existing: browEyeDistance)
markers.definition: Lower brow margin to upper lid margin (ps) at the mid-pupil line
markers.ethnicNorms: Vogue models (mixed): height at mid-pupil 0.36 ± 0.16 × PFL. Arab: not found
markers.perception: Regardless of race, attractive composites had lower brows than average [R28]. Women want the brow's lower border *at* the orbital rim at mid-pupil [R26]. Raters under 30 prefer lower brows; over 50 prefer arched [R27]

markers.name: Medial brow height
markers.definition: Lower brow margin above the endocanthion
markers.ethnicNorms: Vogue: 0.53 ± 0.17 × PFL; celebrities: medial canthus to medial brow 1.73 ± 0.36 cm M, 1.86 ± 0.33 cm F
markers.perception: Women want the medial brow just below the orbital rim [R26]

markers.name: Lateral brow / tail height
markers.definition: Lower brow margin above the exocanthion
markers.perception: Most dimorphic brow height (F > M). Women want the brow several mm above the rim at the lateral canthus; men want a lower tail [R26]. ME consensus: elevated, arched brows; lateral flare preferred in Egypt and Iran [R7]

markers.name: Brow length
markers.definition: Head-to-tail brow length
markers.normMale: 3D lower-brow length Caucasian 69.54 ± 5.79; Chinese 68.54 ± 7.02; celeb total 5.10 ± 0.38 cm
markers.ethnicNorms: Vogue: brow width 1.64 ± 0.24 × PFL (stable over a century)
markers.perception: Attractive males have longer total and medial brows (p < .001) [R15]

markers.name: Brow apex location (existing: browPeak)
markers.definition: Position of the brow peak along the brow (medial → lateral) and relative to the eye
markers.formula: medial segment / total length; apex x relative to limbus/ex
markers.ethnicNorms: South Asian: apex between lateral limbus and lateral canthus most common (four apex types); MSI vs South Indian women differ in apex–lateral-limbus distance (values paywalled)
markers.perception: Brow peak "just medial to the lateral canthus" is desired in both sexes [R26]

markers.name: Brow inclination angles (existing: browTilt, browArch)
markers.definition: Angles at the medial brow point, apex and lateral point relative to the inter-pupillary line
markers.perception: Celebrity brow angles did not differ by sex [R15]. Young raters dislike strongly arched brows [R27]

markers.name: Brow thickness (existing: browThickness)
markers.definition: Vertical brow thickness at the apex/mid-pupil
markers.ethnicNorms: ME consensus: thicker brows preferred by most Middle-Eastern women [R7]
markers.perception: Brow thickness was among the most salient cues to attractiveness and masculinity (conjoint study, N = 922); thicker brows were marginally *more* attractive in female faces [R29]

markers.name: Brow tail end relative to lateral canthus
markers.definition: Distance from exocanthion to the lateral brow end
markers.perception: n.s. by sex [R15]

markers.name: Medial brow start (horizontal)
markers.definition: Horizontal position of the brow head relative to the endocanthion / alar vertical
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Inter-brow distance
markers.definition: Gap between the two brow heads
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Alar (nasal) width
markers.definition: Alare to alare
markers.normMale: Saudi 36.85 ± 3.16; Saudi 3D 38.19 ± 3.10; Gulf Arabs (Dharap) 37.1 ± 3.4; Yemeni 34.1 ± 2.21; NAW 34.9 ± 2.1
markers.ethnicNorms: Farkas 2005: Egyptian 32.4/29.3, Turkish 36.8/32.9, Iranian 35.3/32.1, Chinese 39.2/37.2, African-American 44.1/40.1; Kenyan 43.2/40.7; Black SA F 42.9. Saudi widths lie between whites and Chinese [R9]. Middle-Eastern width ≈ NAW but height greater [R1]
markers.perception: ME consensus: a small, narrow, straight nose is most desired; "wide nostrils" are a common Egyptian complaint [R7]

markers.name: Alar / intercanthal width (existing: noseWidthToIntercanthal)
markers.definition: Nose width relative to eye spacing (orbito-nasal canon)
markers.ethnicNorms: Saudi: al-al > en-en in 92.4 % M, 56 % F; Black SA F 124.5 ± 12.2 %; Korean-American: equal in 1 % vs 41 % of NAW; Southern Chinese: 76 % nose > intercanthal vs 37.9 % in whites (R47)
markers.perception: Canon "equal" found in only 40 % of NAW [R41]. Do not use 1.0 as the ideal for Gulf users

markers.name: Alar / bizygomatic width (canon VIII)
markers.definition: Nose width relative to face width
markers.perception: Canon (¼) held in 37 % of NAW [R41]

markers.name: Nasal index (frontal)
markers.definition: Nose width relative to nose height
markers.ethnicNorms: Farkas 2005 Chinese 73.3/72.0; Kenyan 84.7/85.5 (RoM). Turkish young adults: published in Tekin 2026 (abstract not read)
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Nose height / face height (existing: noseLengthToFace)
markers.definition: Nasion–subnasale relative to nasion–menton
markers.ethnicNorms: Middle-Eastern groups have greater nose height than NAW [R1]; Saudi N-Sn/zy-zy 0.437 ± 0.047 M, 0.438 ± 0.074 F
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Alar base width (subalare)
markers.definition: Width at the alar insertions (sbal–sbal)
markers.ethnicNorms: Black SA F base width 39.5 ± 3.2 (different landmark)
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Alar flare
markers.definition: Alar width minus alar-crease width
markers.normFemale: NAW 0.9 mm (derived); Black SA F 1.7 ± 0.9 mm
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Tip (lobule) width
markers.definition: Width of the lobule at the domes
markers.photo: basal for norm; frontal proxy unvalidated
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Nasal root width
markers.definition: Maxillofrontale to maxillofrontale
markers.ethnicNorms: Al-Qattan measured 25 Saudi nasal variables (values paywalled)
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Nasal dorsum / bridge width
markers.definition: Width between dorsal aesthetic lines at mid-dorsum
markers.perception: ME consensus: depressed or wide bridge is an Egyptian complaint; a dorsal hump is an Iranian one [R7]

markers.name: Nostril show (frontal)
markers.definition: Amount of nostril visible from the front (tip rotation proxy)
markers.perception: Retroussé (upturned) tip is undesirable in Jeddah/western Saudi [R7]

markers.name: Nasal deviation
markers.definition: Lateral deviation of dorsum/tip from the facial midline
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Mouth (intercommissural) width
markers.definition: Cheilion to cheilion, lips at rest
markers.ethnicNorms: Kenyan 55.9/52.0; Chinese F 45.38 (20s) → 49.51 (50s). Farkas 2005: mouth width "identical to NAW" in 99.7 % of groups
markers.perception: Mouth width was among the strongest 3D correlates of attractiveness (Galantucci 2016, cited in R43). Mouth widens with age [R36]

markers.name: Mouth / nose width (existing: mouthToNoseWidth)
markers.definition: Intercommissural width relative to alar width (canon 1.5)
markers.ethnicNorms: Kenyan: canon 1.5 met in 6 %/11 %; Kenyan nose–mouth index (al/ch ×100) 77.3/78.7 vs NAW 65.3/63.3 (derived)
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Mouth / intercanthal width
markers.definition: Mouth width relative to eye spacing
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Mouth width / interpupillary distance
markers.definition: Commissure width relative to pupil spacing
markers.perception: Classical "commissures at medial limbus" rule (Powell & Humphreys 1984; book not accessed)

markers.name: Mouth / face width
markers.definition: Mouth width relative to bizygomatic width
markers.perception: see lip-mouth-width

markers.name: Upper vermilion height
markers.definition: Labrale superius to stomion
markers.normMale: Jazan Saudi 14.38 (400, SD n/a); Kenyan 13.7 ± 1.3; NAW 7.8 (derived)
markers.normFemale: Jazan 13.78; Kenyan 13.4 ± 0.9; NAW 8.7 (derived); Black SA 11.0 ± 2.0; Chinese 8.10 ± 1.40 (20s)
markers.perception: Thins with age: Chinese 8.10 → 6.57 mm from 20s to 50s [R36]. Ageing narrows vermilions [R39]

markers.name: Lower vermilion height
markers.definition: Stomion to labrale inferius
markers.ethnicNorms: Persian F 9.18 ± 1.61. Jazan Saudi: upper vermilion thinner than lower in both sexes
markers.perception: Declines with age (Chinese 9.79 → 8.57) [R36]

markers.name: Upper : lower vermilion ratio (existing: lipRatio)
markers.definition: Upper vermilion height over lower
markers.ethnicNorms: ME consensus: preferred upper:lower fullness differs by subregion; in Jeddah/western Saudi an upper lip *thinner* than the lower is undesirable [R7]
markers.perception: Popenko: 1:2 (0.5) most attractive, 2:1 least (white female faces, 428 raters) [R33]. Heidekrueger: 60 % of 1011 respondents chose 1:1 [R35]. The current code target 0.62 is not traceable to these sources

markers.name: Total vermilion height / mouth width (existing: lipFullness)
markers.definition: Lip fullness index
markers.perception: Fuller lips in Saudi women (p < .001). Fuller lips preferred in ME women [R7]

markers.name: Upper lip height / lower-third split (existing: lipChinRatio)
markers.definition: Subnasale–stomion relative to stomion–menton
markers.normFemale: Egyptian sn-sto 32.07 ± 2.25 % and sto-gn 67.93 ± 2.25 % of lower third (ratio ≈ 0.47); Jazan 20.66 ± 4.12 mm; NAW 20.1 ± 2.0 mm; Persian 21.99
markers.perception: Ageing lengthens the upper lip [R36]

markers.name: Philtrum (cutaneous upper lip) length
markers.definition: Subnasale to labrale superius
markers.perception: Age marker: lengthens with age (p = .001 Persian; Chinese) [R6, R36]

markers.name: Upper vermilion / upper lip height
markers.definition: Share of the upper lip that is red lip
markers.perception: Higher upper-vermilion / mouth–nose distance ratio in attractive female (p < .001) and male (p < .05) perioral regions; also higher upper-vermilion / chin–nose ratio [R34]

markers.name: Lower vermilion / chin–mouth distance
markers.definition: Lower red-lip height relative to stomion–menton
markers.normFemale: Black SA lower vermilion : lower lip 0.685 ± 0.120 (different denominator)
markers.perception: Attractive female perioral regions have a higher ratio than attractive male ones (p < .05) [R34]

markers.name: Philtrum width
markers.definition: Distance between the philtral columns at the vermilion border (crista philtri)
markers.ethnicNorms: Stable with age in Chinese women [R36]
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Cupid's bow definition
markers.definition: Peak height and angle of the cupid's bow
markers.normFemale: not found (Chong 2021 reports vermilion angles but their geometry was not extracted)
markers.perception: Ageing flattens the vermilion border [R36]

markers.name: Mouth-corner tilt (existing: mouthCornerTilt)
markers.definition: Elevation of the cheilia relative to the stomion
markers.normFemale: Korean women: 5-type classification; Type IIb most common (51.1 % / 37.3 %) and increases with age; Type Ia/Ib decline with age (n = 820 + 496)
markers.perception: Treating the corners to create an upward angle signals youth (ME consensus) [R7]

markers.name: Lip surface area / lower facial third
markers.definition: Red-lip area as a share of the lower-third area
markers.perception: Most attractive: 53.5 % larger than baseline surface area, 1:2 upper:lower ratio, 9.6 % of the lower third [R33]

markers.name: Bizygomatic width
markers.definition: Zygion to zygion (face width)
markers.normFemale: NAW 130.0; Saudi 3D 128.94 ± 8.23; Egyptian 119.21 ± 8.15 (rises with age, p = .001); Persian 134.16 ± 10.30; celeb 13.05 ± 0.75 cm; Black SA 139.2 ± 6.8
markers.perception: Wider in attractive men than women [R15]. Narrowing the face is undesirable for ME women (unlike Asia) [R7]

markers.name: Midface length index
markers.definition: Glabella–subnasale as a share of glabella–gnathion
markers.perception: ME consensus: a flat midface is a common complaint in women under 40 [R7]

markers.name: Cheekbone prominence (frontal width proxy)
markers.definition: Face width at the zygoma relative to widths at the temples and at mouth level
markers.landmarks: zy ≈234/454, temples 54/284, contour at mouth level
markers.perception: In a conjoint study cheekbone prominence was *less* salient than brows/jaw [R29]. ME consensus: laterally full, defined cheekbones [R7]. Cunningham 1986 (high cheekbones; not accessed)

markers.name: Cheekbone height
markers.definition: Vertical level of maximal midface width relative to the eye–mouth span
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Malar fullness / submalar hollowness
markers.definition: Visible anterior cheek volume vs submalar shadow
markers.ethnicNorms: Gulf (Bedouin influence): full cheeks and round face preferred; urban Kuwait: defined submalar hollow; ME faces "heavier" and prone to sagging [R7]
markers.perception: ME consensus as stated [R7]

markers.name: Bigonial width
markers.definition: Gonion to gonion
markers.normFemale: NAW 94.5; Saudi 3D 116.26 ± 9.68; Egyptian 103.94 ± 8.90 (rises with age, p = .007); Persian 107.99 ± 7.81; celeb 11.13 ± 0.70 cm
markers.perception: Wider in attractive men (p < .0001) [R15]

markers.name: Bigonial / bizygomatic (existing: jawToFaceWidth)
markers.definition: Jaw width relative to cheek width
markers.normFemale: celeb 0.852 (from 1.174 ± 0.048); NAW 0.73; Kenyan 0.74; Egyptian 0.87; Persian 0.80; Saudi 3D 0.90 (RoM)
markers.perception: Jaw prominence was a salient cue; a masculine jaw is more attractive on male faces and a feminine jaw on female faces [R29]. Mandibular contour was decisive for attractiveness in Indian women [R40]. ME consensus: well-defined jawline; avoid narrowing the lower face [R7]

markers.name: Mandible width / biocular width
markers.definition: Jaw width relative to outer-canthal width
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Lower face height / mandible width
markers.definition: sn–me relative to go–go
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Face height / bigonial width
markers.definition: Trichion–menton (or n–me) relative to bigonial width
markers.perception: Attractive females approximated 1.618 [R15]; general phi claims are criticised [R42]

markers.name: Lower face height / face height
markers.definition: sn–me relative to n–me
markers.perception: Attractive Iranian women had longer lower faces (Khosravanifard 2013, cited in R7)

markers.name: Chin height
markers.definition: Labrale inferius to menton (or sublabiale–gnathion)
markers.normMale: Saudi 3D li-me 30.84 ± 3.84; NAW sl-gn 33.1 (derived); Kenyan fml-me 36.5 ± 3.1
markers.ethnicNorms: Saudi 3D chin height / mandibular body length 0.34 ± 0.05 (both sexes)
markers.perception: Attractive Iranian women had lips closer to the middle of the chin–nose distance (cited in R7)

markers.name: Chin width (existing: chinWidthToMouth)
markers.definition: Width of the chin at the mental tubercles relative to mouth width
markers.perception: ME consensus: a pointed, moderately projected chin is preferred in women; an under-projected chin is a common complaint [R7]

markers.name: Mandibular outline (frontal)
markers.definition: Shape class of the lower-face contour (tapered/V, oval, square) and gonial flare
markers.ethnicNorms: ME consensus: oval/round faces preferred; Asian narrowing trends not wanted [R7]
markers.perception: Mandibular shape decisive in Indian female attractiveness [R40]

markers.name: Ear length
markers.definition: Superaurale to subaurale
markers.photo: frontal, ears uncovered (often not the case in the Gulf)
markers.normMale: not found (adult Arab; values not in abstract)
markers.ethnicNorms: Farkas 2005: ear height ≈ NAW in 99.7 % of comparisons [R1]
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Ear length / nose height (naso-aural canon)
markers.definition: Ear length compared with nose height
markers.perception: The naso-aural canons were among nine neoclassical canons tested; the canons "do not represent average proportions" [R41]

markers.name: Ear protrusion (frontal proxy)
markers.definition: Lateral projection of the helix beyond the head contour as seen from the front
markers.normMale: Arabian ears: helix–mastoid distance ≥ 20.5 mm (sensitivity 0.84) and concha–mastoid angle ≥ 60.5° (AUC 0.808, specificity 0.88) predicted perceived prominence; men have larger concha–mastoid angles
markers.normFemale: same cut-offs; women showed mild natural asymmetry
markers.perception: Perceived prominence rose with helix–mastoid distance and concha–mastoid angle, especially in males and younger people [R11]

markers.name: Ear vertical position
markers.definition: Superaurale level vs brow line and subaurale level vs subnasale
markers.perception: Classical rule (Powell & Humphreys 1984) not accessed

markers.name: Ear height asymmetry
markers.definition: Difference in sa/sba levels L vs R
markers.normFemale: Arabian women: mild natural asymmetry (no values in abstract)
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Facial convexity angle (Legan & Burstone)
markers.definition: Profile convexity excluding the nose
markers.perception: Iranian sample: a more convex soft-tissue profile was associated with higher profile beauty scores (β = 0.710 for facial convexity angle; Ghorbanyjavadpour 2019)
markers.sources: Legan & Burstone 1980; Celebi 2013; AlBarakati 2011; Abutayyem 2021; Ghorbanyjavadpour 2019

markers.name: Total facial convexity (including the nose)
markers.definition: Convexity angle with the nose included
markers.normMale: not found (primary Caucasian norm not accessed)
markers.ethnicNorms: Emirati M 127.48 ± 4.78°, F 136.85 ± 8.03° (n 91/85). Saudi: females have a greater total convexity angle than males (Hashim 2003, values not in abstract)
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Soft-tissue profile angle
markers.definition: Convexity measured from N' instead of G
markers.ethnicNorms: Emirati M 156.91 ± 6.92°, F 133.80 ± 5.51° (female value looks implausible)
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Soft-tissue facial angle (Holdaway)
markers.definition: Inclination of the N'–Pg' line to FH. Indicates chin prominence
markers.perception: Syrian Class II males: the most attractive had a larger N-Pog/FH angle (more prominent chin) (Mortada 2023). Iranian: β = −0.348 for soft-tissue facial angle (Ghorbanyjavadpour 2019)

markers.name: Z-angle (Merrifield)
markers.definition: Angle between FH and the profile line tangent to Pg' and the more protrusive lip
markers.perception: Iranian: β = 0.557 (Ghorbanyjavadpour 2019)

markers.name: Maxillary prognathism (Legan)
markers.definition: Horizontal distance from a G vertical to Sn
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Mandibular prognathism (Legan)
markers.definition: Horizontal distance from a G vertical to Pg'
markers.perception: see the chin markers

markers.name: Vertical height ratio (G-Sn : Sn-Me')
markers.definition: Midface to lower-face height
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Nasal-to-gnathic third ratio
markers.definition: N'-Sn : Sn-Me'
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Lower-face proportion
markers.definition: Lower face height as a share of total face height
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Forehead inclination
markers.definition: Slope of the forehead outline from G up to a point near Tr against TV. Sloping vs upright forehead
markers.landmarks: G, upper forehead point (Tr if visible), TV
markers.perception: not found (a sex-dimorphic trait per surgical texts, but no quantitative perception study was found)

markers.name: Glabellar / forehead projection
markers.definition: How far G projects relative to N' (brow-ridge prominence)
markers.formula: horizontal distance G − N' [mm], or nasion depth (see nose-radix-depth)
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Nasolabial angle
markers.definition: Angle between the columella tangent and the upper-lip tangent. Also the main clinical proxy for tip rotation
markers.ethnicNorms: Saudi M 96.23 ± 12.74°, F 104.19 ± 11.92° (n 30/32; Aljabaa); Saudi pooled 106.02 ± 11.01° (AlBarakati). Emirati M 117.62 ± 10.48°, F 120.13 ± 10.72°; Emirati (Al Zain, via Saadeh) M 122, F 116. Kuwaiti (via Saadeh) M 109.4, F 111.3. Qatari F 99.33. Lebanese M 109.03 ± 12.05°, F 109.15 ± 8.84°. Turkish M 105.7 ± 9.5°, F 108.4 ± 7.4°. Syrian (photo) M 103.46 ± 12.31°, F 100.94 ± 10.07°
markers.perception: 3D textured faces: 90° most attractive for the male image; historical "ideal" 90–120° (El-Habbash 2025). Iranian: a larger NLA was associated with higher profile beauty (β = 0.546; Ghorbanyjavadpour 2019)
markers.sources: Legan & Burstone 1980; Aljabaa 2019; AlBarakati 2011; Abutayyem 2021; Saadeh 2025; Celebi 2013; Torbey 2024; El-Habbash 2025

markers.name: Nasofrontal angle
markers.definition: Angle at N' between the glabella tangent and the nasal dorsum
markers.perception: Naini 2016 (male silhouette): about 130° ideal, 127–142° acceptable; <115° (simulated hump) least attractive. Surgery threshold ≤121° (patients), ≤124° (lay), ≤118° (clinicians), and ≥148°
markers.sources: Powell & Humphreys 1984; Aljabaa 2019; Saadeh 2025; Torbey 2024; Naini 2016a

markers.name: Nasofacial angle
markers.definition: Angle between the facial plane (G–Pg') and the nasal dorsum
markers.perception: Naini 2016 (silhouette): about 30° ideal, 27–36° acceptable, outside 21–42° very unattractive; surgery thresholds ≥39° and ≤24°. Iranian β = 0.259

markers.name: Nasomental angle
markers.definition: Angle between the nasal dorsum and the Prn–Pg' line
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Tip projection: Goode ratio
markers.definition: Tip projection (perpendicular from Prn to the N'–AC line) divided by nasal length (N'–Prn)
markers.perception: Iranian women: lay raters preferred Goode-level projection; surgeons and artists preferred Crumley 2 (Mohebbi 2016). Brazil: Crumley 2 most chosen (48.2%) (Beduschi 2026)

markers.name: Tip projection: Crumley & Lanser triangle
markers.definition: Right triangle N'–AC–Prn; the sides should follow a fixed 3:4:5 proportion (Crumley 2)
markers.formula: proportions of the sides of N'–AC–Prn
markers.normMale: "3:4:5" (primary abstract not accessed; method described in Mohebbi 2016)
markers.perception: as for Goode (Mohebbi 2016)

markers.name: Tip projection: Simons ratio
markers.definition: Sn–tip length compared with upper-lip length (Sn–Ls)
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Tip projection: Baum / Powell-modified ratio
markers.definition: Nasal length (N'–Sn) divided by tip projection (perpendicular from Prn to the N'–Sn line)
markers.perception: Iranian: the Powell & Humphreys projection was the least preferred by all three rater groups (Mohebbi 2016)

markers.name: Tip projection: Byrd & Hobar ratio
markers.definition: Sn-to-tip projection as a share of upper-lip length
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Nasal tip projection angle (Aljabaa)
markers.definition: Internal angle between true horizontal and the dorsal nasal line
markers.ethnicNorms: Saudi lower than the New Zealand sample (Aljabaa)
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Tip rotation (columellar inclination)
markers.definition: Columella inclination against true vertical. The nasolabial angle is usually used as the rotation proxy
markers.normMale: not found as a separate norm
markers.perception: Iranian: "higher tips" were associated with better profiles (Ghorbanyjavadpour 2019)

markers.name: Nasal length (N'–Prn)
markers.definition: Straight-line length of the nose
markers.ethnicNorms: Saudi noses longer than the New Zealand sample
markers.perception: Iranian: "less prominent noses" were associated with better profiles

markers.name: Nasal height (N'–Sn)
markers.definition: Vertical height of the nose
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Nose prominence (Holdaway / angular)
markers.definition: How far the nose stands out from the upper lip or face
markers.formula: Holdaway: Prn to a line perpendicular to FH through Ls [mm]; angular: ∠Prn-N'-Sn
markers.ethnicNorms: Lebanese M 13.44 ± 2.35, F 13.06 ± 2.36 mm. Emirati ∠Prn-N'-Sn M 20.0 ± 2.22°, F 20.73 ± 6.29°. Saudi nasal depth Prn–VP M 24.50 ± 4.84, F 22.98 ± 4.64 mm
markers.perception: Naini 2016b (excess prominence least attractive); Iranian: β = −0.245

markers.name: Dorsal hump / dorsum shape
markers.definition: Deviation of the dorsal outline from the straight N'–SupT line (convex hump, straight, concave/scooped)
markers.formula: maximum perpendicular deviation of the outline from N'–SupT [mm or % of nasal length]; categorical
markers.perception: Naini 2016a: a reduced nasofrontal angle, which simulates a hump, was least attractive

markers.name: Supratip break
markers.definition: Small concavity just above the tip lobule (supratip point to dorsal line)
markers.formula: Aljabaa: angle between the dorsal plane and the supratip plane; or depth [mm]
markers.ethnicNorms: Saudi larger than the New Zealand sample
markers.perception: Facial-feminisation raters: a more acute supratip angle was rated more feminine and attractive (Ching 2021)

markers.name: Columella show
markers.definition: Columella visible below the alar rim in profile
markers.formula: maximum vertical distance between the alar rim and the columella [mm]
markers.normMale: not found (not verified in an accessed primary source)
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Radix (nasion) depth / position
markers.definition: How deep N' sits behind the G–Prn line (radix projection)
markers.landmarks: G, N', Prn (or the corneal plane)
markers.formula: perpendicular distance from N' to the G–Prn line [mm]; Byrd & Hobar's radix projection is measured from the corneal plane
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Upper lip to E-line (Ricketts)
markers.definition: Distance from Ls to the esthetic line Prn–Pg' (negative = behind the line)
markers.normMale: −4 ± 2 mm (Ricketts norm as tabulated in Saadeh 2025)
markers.ethnicNorms: Saudi (Uysal, via Saadeh) M −3.8, F −4.1. Turkish M −6.1, F −5.8. Kuwaiti M −5.66, F −5.4. Emirati M −5.88 ± 3.56, F −1.80 ± 4.03. Qatari F +3.32. Lebanese M −4.87 ± 1.81, F −5.12 ± 1.64 mm
markers.perception: Naini 2021: −12 to −16 mm and 0 to +4 mm cut median attractiveness below 4/7; protrusive lips were viewed as more attractive than retrusive ones. Middle-Eastern raters preferred lips about 1 mm ahead of the Ricketts norm (Sadek & Alali 2025). Iranian β = 0.691
markers.sources: Ricketts 1968; Saadeh 2025; Uysal 2011; Abutayyem 2021; Naini 2021; Sadek & Alali 2025; Ghorbanyjavadpour 2019

markers.name: Lower lip to E-line (Ricketts)
markers.definition: Distance from Li to Prn–Pg'
markers.ethnicNorms: Saudi (Uysal, via Saadeh) M −0.3, F −1.7. Turkish M −3.4, F −2.6. Kuwaiti M −3.11, F −0.99. Emirati M −2.23 ± 4.41, F −1.32 ± 4.42. Lebanese M −2.29 ± 1.84, F −2.79 ± 1.74 mm
markers.perception: as for the upper lip; Iranian β = −0.674 (less prominent lower lip preferred)

markers.name: Steiner S-line
markers.definition: Lips relative to the line from Pg' to the midpoint of the nasal "S" curve (columella–Sn)
markers.formula: signed distances of Ls and Li [mm]
markers.normMale: lips ideally touching the line (0 mm) — Steiner's original not accessed
markers.perception: not found
markers.sources: Steiner 1953 (DOI verified; S-line originally described in later Steiner papers, not accessed)

markers.name: Lip protrusion to the Sn–Pg' line (Burstone B-line)
markers.definition: Ls and Li relative to the Sn–Pg' line
markers.perception: Iranian: lower-lip protrusion β = −0.342. Iranian lay raters: normal ±2 mm favoured, moderate retrusion least attractive (Golfeshan 2024)
markers.sources: Burstone 1967; Legan & Burstone 1980; Celebi 2013; Saadeh 2025; Abutayyem 2021; Golfeshan 2024

markers.name: Holdaway H-angle
markers.definition: Angle between the H-line (Pg'–Ls tangent) and the soft-tissue facial line N'–Pg'
markers.normMale: 10 ± 4° (as tabulated in Saadeh 2025); Holdaway described about 7–15° as acceptable depending on convexity
markers.ethnicNorms: Saudi (Uysal, via Saadeh) M 16.3, F 15.4. Turkish 12.7 / 12.7. Emirati M 14.56 ± 4.46, F 12.99 ± 3.84. Lebanese M 13.45 ± 3.18, F 12.71 ± 2.83. Malay F 15.75 ± 4.16
markers.perception: Iranian: β = −0.360

markers.name: Lower lip to H-line
markers.definition: Distance from Li to the H-line
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Subnasale to H-line
markers.definition: Distance from Sn to the H-line (upper-lip support)
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Upper lip inclination
markers.definition: Angle of the upper-lip tangent (Sn–Ls) to true horizontal
markers.perception: Naini 2015 (silhouette): 79–85° ideal, 73–88° acceptable; treatment desired at ≥91–94° or ≤64°

markers.name: Superior labial sulcus depth
markers.definition: Depth of the upper-lip concavity (soft-tissue A point) behind a line from Sn to Ls
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Vertical lip–chin ratio (Sn-Stms : Stmi-Me')
markers.definition: Upper-lip height relative to lower-lip-plus-chin height
markers.perception: Iranian: Sn-Stms:Stms-Me' β = −0.372

markers.name: Lip thickness / vermilion eversion
markers.definition: Profile thickness and fullness of the vermilion
markers.formula: horizontal vermilion depth from the vermilion border to Ls/Li [mm]. The ceph values below are measured to the teeth, which a photo cannot see
markers.normMale: Ceph (to the incisor): Lebanese UL at the vermilion border 13.37 ± 1.99, LL 14.57 ± 1.50 mm
markers.perception: Thick, mildly protruded lips were preferred by African raters; Middle-Eastern raters preferred the +1 mm position (Sadek & Alali 2025)
markers.automatable: LMK (vermilion border) [mm]; ceph version not reproducible on photos

markers.name: Interlabial gap at rest
markers.definition: Vertical gap between Stms and Stmi with lips relaxed
markers.perception: Iranian: smaller gap better (β = −0.179)

markers.name: Labiomental (mentolabial) angle
markers.definition: Angle between the lower-lip tangent and the chin tangent at Sm
markers.perception: Naini 2017: about 107–118° most attractive; up to 140° acceptable; <98° or >162° very unattractive. Taiwanese students preferred 137° on a Taiwanese face and 117° on a white face (Tseng 2025)

markers.name: Mentolabial sulcus depth
markers.definition: Depth of Sm behind the Li–Pg' line
markers.ethnicNorms: Saudi 4.60 ± 1.23. Turkish M 5.4 ± 1.6, F 5.9 ± 1.6. Yemeni 5.0 ± 1.1. Lebanese inferior sulcus to H-line M 4.91 ± 1.16, F 4.46 ± 1.24
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Chin projection: Gonzalez-Ulloa zero meridian
markers.definition: Pg' position relative to a line through N' perpendicular to FH
markers.normMale: ideal: chin on the line (no numeric SD)
markers.perception: Chin retrusion was less penalised than protrusion (Modarai 2013)

markers.name: Lower lip–chin prominence angle (Naini)
markers.definition: Angle of the line from the most prominent point of the lower lip to Pg', measured against true vertical
markers.normMale: ideal ≈ 0° (Pg' on or just behind the TV through the lower lip)
markers.perception: 15° retrusion to −5° prominence acceptable; surgery desired beyond −15° prominence or >25° retrusion (Naini 2019a). Chinese raters: female best at a lip–chin angle of 20°, male 10–20° (Gui 2026, different definition)

markers.name: Chin prominence (Legan mandibular prognathism, G-vertical)
markers.definition: Same as prof-mandibular-prognathism; also available scale-free as the facial-convexity angle
markers.perception: Iranian: "more protruding chins" improved profile beauty (Ghorbanyjavadpour 2019). Syrian males: more chin protrusion in the most attractive (Mortada 2023)

markers.name: Gonial angle (soft-tissue estimate)
markers.definition: Angle between the posterior ramus tangent and the mandibular lower-border tangent, read from the soft-tissue jaw contour
markers.normMale: not found (no validated soft-tissue photo norm)
markers.ethnicNorms: not found (Ayoub 2009 Lebanese gonial dimorphism is radiographic; not accessed)
markers.perception: A more obtuse gonial angle was judged more feminine (Ching 2021)
markers.automatable: LMK/REV (the ramus contour is inside the silhouette; needs shading or 3D)

markers.name: Mandibular plane inclination (soft tissue)
markers.definition: Slope of the jaw's lower border (Me' toward the gonial angle) against true horizontal
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Ramus visibility / posterior jaw definition
markers.definition: Whether the posterior ramus border and angle can be seen as a distinct edge from the earlobe region down
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Jawline (inferior mandibular border) definition
markers.definition: How sharply the lower mandibular border separates from the neck. Ellenbogen's first criterion
markers.formula: REV grade; proxy: curvature or contrast along the border and the CMA
markers.perception: Part of Ellenbogen's youthful-neck criteria

markers.name: Cervicomental angle (Ellenbogen)
markers.definition: Angle between the submental (lower-jaw) tangent and the anterior neck tangent
markers.perception: Target range in neck rejuvenation; a widening angle signals ageing or submental fat

markers.name: Submental-cervical angle (Naini)
markers.definition: Angle between the submental and cervical tangents on an idealised profile (operationally close to the CMA)
markers.perception: 90–105° acceptable; up to 120° slightly unattractive (lay, clinicians) or very unattractive (patients); 125–130° very unattractive for all. Surgery thresholds 110° (patients), 115° (lay), 125° (clinicians) (Naini 2016c)

markers.name: Mentocervical angle (Powell & Humphreys)
markers.definition: Angle between the facial plane (G–Pg') and the submental tangent (Me'–C)
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Lower face–throat angle (Legan)
markers.definition: Angle between the Sn–Gn' line and the throat line Gn'–C
markers.perception: Thai raters: the lip–chin–throat angle (a related angle) correlated with attractiveness (quadratic; Pornsirianand 2025)

markers.name: Lower vertical height–depth ratio (Sn-Gn' : C-Gn')
markers.definition: Lower-face height relative to throat (submental) length
markers.ethnicNorms: Saudi 1.14 ± 0.20 (Saudis have a shorter neck distance than European-Americans). Turkish M 1.6 ± 1.4, F 1.4 ± 0.4
markers.perception: Throat length correlated with attractiveness for lay and orthodontist raters (Pornsirianand 2025)

markers.name: Submental length (throat length)
markers.definition: Length of the submental contour from Me' (or Gn') back to C
markers.perception: Ideal about 50 mm (range 40–75 mm); ≤30 mm unattractive; surgery cut-offs ≤25 mm (clinicians), ≤30 or 95 mm (patients and lay). Should fall between lower lip–chin height and lower-face height (Naini 2020)

markers.name: Neck definition (Ellenbogen criteria)
markers.definition: Composite of distinct mandibular border, subhyoid depression, visible thyroid-cartilage bulge, visible anterior sternocleidomastoid border, and CMA in range
markers.landmarks: lower border, C, thyroid prominence, SCM
markers.perception: Defines the "youthful neck"; criteria simplified to three in later literature (O'Daniel 2026)

markers.name: Submental fullness ("double chin") proxy
markers.definition: Convexity or bulging of the submental contour between Me' and C
markers.formula: maximum outward deviation of the outline from the straight line Me'–C [mm or % of Me'–C], plus the CMA
markers.perception: not found (validated clinical grading scales exist but were not retrieved)

markers.name: Neck length
markers.definition: Vertical length of the visible anterior neck
markers.landmarks: C or Me', sternal notch / clothing line
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Ear length (sa–sba)
markers.definition: Total ear height
markers.ethnicNorms: Saudi Eastern Province values shown. Indian men had the smallest ear lengths in a cross-ethnic comparison (Purkait 2007)
markers.perception: Ears keep growing with age (Sforza 2009; Purkait 2007), so ear length is a possible age cue; no attractiveness data found

markers.name: Ear width (pra–pa)
markers.definition: Ear breadth
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Ear index (width/length)
markers.definition: Ear shape ratio
markers.normMale: not found as a ratio in the accessed source (derive from Hiware means: about 0.50 M, 0.55 F; derived, not published)
markers.perception: The ratio falls with age in both sexes (Sforza 2009, n 843)

markers.name: Ear axis inclination
markers.definition: Tilt of the ear's long axis from true vertical (often compared with the nasal dorsum line)
markers.ethnicNorms: Japanese children: the long axis is not parallel to the nasal dorsum (secondary snippet only)
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Ear top level vs brow
markers.definition: Vertical offset of sa from the eyebrow (or G) level
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Ear bottom level vs nasal base
markers.definition: Vertical offset of sba from Sn (nasal-base level)
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Ear protrusion (auriculocephalic angle)
markers.definition: Angle between the helix plane and the mastoid or scalp surface
markers.normMale: commonly cited <25–30° (clinical and secondary sources; no adult mean ± SD found)
markers.perception: Prominent ear (otoplasty) threshold usually set above 30° or >2 cm helix–mastoid (secondary)
markers.automatable: LMK (frontal / back view); profile cannot measure it

markers.name: Helix–mastoid distance
markers.definition: Distance from the helical rim to the scalp at mid-ear
markers.ethnicNorms: Otoplasty review: pre-operative mean 27.1 mm, 15.4 mm after surgery (Kaleeny 2026)
markers.perception: prominence is treated surgically

markers.name: Lobule height
markers.definition: Vertical lobule length
markers.perception: The lobule contributes most to age-related ear elongation (Purkait 2007)

markers.name: Lobule width
markers.definition: Horizontal lobule breadth
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Lobule attachment
markers.definition: Free vs attached lobule
markers.normMale: Saudi lobule-type score M 0.51 ± 0.502 (coding not stated in accessed text)
markers.ethnicNorms: 10-country student sample: lobule and helix forms differ by origin (Bakici 2026)
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Ear AP position (nasion–ear distance)
markers.definition: Horizontal distance from N' to the ear (tragion region)
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Buccal corridor ratio
markers.definition: Dark space between the buccal teeth and the mouth corners, as a share of smile width
markers.landmarks: Ch–Ch, most lateral visible tooth (or canines)
markers.formula: Moore: (Ch–Ch − visible dentition width)/(Ch–Ch) × 100; Ismail uses (C–C)/(Ch–Ch) × 100
markers.perception: Lay raters (n 30): broad smile (2% corridor) beat 10, 15, 22 and 28% (Moore 2005). Japanese raters: scores fell to a clinically significant level from 10% to 25% (Ioi 2009). Excess corridors still acceptable more than 70% of the time (Parekh 2007)

markers.name: Gingival display in smile
markers.definition: Gingiva visible above the maxillary central incisors (or lip coverage of the crown)
markers.landmarks: upper-lip lower border, gingival margin, incisal edge
markers.formula: [mm] (+ gingiva / − lip covers crown); or high / average / low category
markers.perception: Lay raters noticed gingiva-to-lip distance at 4 mm, orthodontists at 2 mm (Kokich 1999); 3 mm rated unattractive by orthodontists and lay raters (Kokich 2006). Saudi raters: 1–2 mm lip coverage most attractive, 4 mm gingiva least (Alaqeely 2023); ≤3 mm attractive, 5 mm least (Alfaifi 2026). Saudi dentists were stricter than lay raters (Talic 2013)
markers.sources: Kokich 1999; Kokich 2006; Alaqeely 2023; Alfaifi 2026; Talic 2013; Ismail 2026

markers.name: Smile arc consonance
markers.definition: Whether the curve of the maxillary incisal edges follows the curve of the lower lip
markers.landmarks: incisal edges of the six front teeth, lower-lip upper border
markers.formula: curvature comparison: consonant / flat / reverse; or curvature difference
markers.perception: Flat arcs acceptable only 50–60% of the time vs 84–95% for ideal or excessive arcs (Parekh 2007). Arc and gingival display jointly affect attractiveness (Kaya & Uyar 2013)

markers.name: Maxillary incisor display at rest
markers.definition: Upper incisor visible below the relaxed upper lip
markers.ethnicNorms: Saudi 3.26 ± 1.96 mm. Turkish M 2.7 ± 1.8, F 3.2 ± 1.9 mm. Yemeni 2.9 ± 1.5
markers.perception: Incisor exposure decreases with age while lower-incisor exposure increases (Vig & Brundo 1978); sex and age values not in the abstract

markers.name: Incisor crown display in smile
markers.definition: Share of the central-incisor crown shown in a posed smile
markers.landmarks: upper lip, incisal edge, gingival margin
markers.normMale: An "average smile" shows about the full length of the maxillary anterior teeth (Tjan 1984; percentages not in the abstract)
markers.perception: see gingival display

markers.name: Upper lip curvature in smile
markers.definition: Shape of the upper lip's lower border in smile (corners up, straight, down)
markers.formula: sign of the vertical offset of the commissures from the lip midpoint; categorical
markers.perception: Iranian: upper-lip curvature (profile measure) β = 0.405 (Ghorbanyjavadpour 2019)

markers.name: Smile index
markers.definition: Width-to-height ratio of the smile (intercommissure width / interlabial height)
markers.landmarks: Ch–Ch, upper and lower lip inner borders
markers.normMale: not found (Ackerman 1998 defines the measure; values not in the abstract)
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Teeth displayed (smile width)
markers.definition: Number of maxillary teeth visible to each side
markers.formula: count, or the most lateral tooth shown
markers.normMale: Average smile shows the six anterior teeth plus premolars (Tjan 1984)
markers.ethnicNorms: Iranian: exposure up to the first molar typical (Bagheri 2025)
markers.perception: links to buccal corridor

markers.name: Smile symmetry (commissure height)
markers.definition: Left–right difference in commissure height and lip elevation
markers.formula: vertical difference [mm] or angle of Ch–Ch to the interpupillary line
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Incisal (occlusal) plane cant
markers.definition: Tilt of the incisal plane against the horizontal or interpupillary line
markers.landmarks: canine cusp tips / incisal edges, interpupillary line
markers.perception: Orthodontists and dentists detected 1 mm; lay raters 3 mm (Kokich 1999). Cant with gingival display studied by Kaya & Uyar 2016

markers.name: Dental midline vs facial midline
markers.definition: Offset of the maxillary central-incisor midline from the facial midline
markers.landmarks: facial midline (N', Sn, philtrum), interincisal point
markers.ethnicNorms: Saudi (Jouf) 78.5% within 2 mm; deviated cases 2.87 ± 0.71 mm
markers.perception: 4 mm needed before orthodontists rated it worse; lay raters missed 4 mm (Kokich 1999). 2 mm → 56% chance a lay rater scores it less attractive (Johnston 1999). Saudi dentists penalised midline shifts more than lay raters (Talic 2013)

markers.name: Duchenne marker (eye involvement)
markers.definition: Whether the smile involves orbicularis oculi (cheek raise, lower-lid bulge, crow's feet)
markers.formula: binary or graded; proxy: change in eye aperture and lateral-canthus wrinkles vs neutral
markers.perception: Defined as the enjoyment smile (Ekman 1990; Frank 1993). A smiling mouth makes Duchenne eyes look brighter (Parovel 2026). No direct attractiveness rating found in accessed abstracts
markers.automatable: LMK (needs a neutral photo for comparison) / REV

markers.name: Incisor inclination in profile smile
markers.definition: Angle of the labial-face tangent of the maxillary incisor crown to true horizontal
markers.ethnicNorms: Saudi raters: −5° (slight retroclination from neutral) most attractive, +15° proclination least (Albwardi 2022)
markers.perception: Proclination was less acceptable than retroclination; treatment recommended beyond 105° (Naini 2019b)

markers.name: Smile in three-quarter view (protrusion)
markers.definition: Overall smile attractiveness in the 45° view, affected by bimaxillary protrusion
markers.perception: Bimaxillary-protrusion smiles were rated less attractive, especially by lay raters. Frontal and three-quarter ratings of the same smile differed. U1-PP correlated most negatively (Almutairi 2015)

markers.name: Ogee curve
markers.definition: Continuous S-shaped contour in the 45° view: convex malar/cheek, then concave submalar, then convex jaw
markers.landmarks: lateral face contour from the zygoma to the mandible
markers.formula: REV, or curvature sign changes along the outline
markers.perception: not found (an aesthetic-medicine concept; no quantitative study found)
markers.automatable: REV / OUT (the 45° outline can be segmented, but there is no norm)

markers.name: Malar prominence (45°)
markers.definition: Anterior and lateral projection of the cheekbone in the oblique view
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Jawline contour (45°)
markers.definition: Continuity and definition of the mandibular border from chin to angle
markers.perception: Ellenbogen first criterion

markers.name: Nasal dorsum aesthetic line (45°)
markers.definition: Smooth brow-to-tip line and dorsal hump visibility in the oblique view
markers.perception: not found

markers.name: Constitutive skin colour (L\*a\*b\*, ITA°)
markers.definition: Mean colour of facial skin (cheek/forehead ROI) in CIELAB, and the Individual Typology Angle
markers.photo: Frontal, no makeup, diffuse light, CCC required, XPL preferred
markers.method: Convert calibrated RGB → CIELAB (D65), ROI mean; ITA° = arctan((L\*−50)/b\*)×180/π
markers.norms: ITA categories (Del Bino 2018, from Chardon 1991 / Del Bino 2006): very light >55°, light 41–55°, intermediate 28–41°, tan 10–28°, brown 10° to −30°, dark <−30° (the minus sign was lost in our text extraction; inferred). No Gulf population ITA norms found
markers.perception: ITA correlates with melanin content (Del Bino 2018). Used as a stratifier; no direct attractiveness link in these sources

markers.name: Skin colour homogeneity / evenness
markers.definition: How uniform the facial skin colour is: the inverse of patchy pigment and redness
markers.photo: As above, CCC + controlled lighting; full-face frontal
markers.method: SD or entropy of L\*/a\*/b\* (or of melanin/haemoglobin maps) across a skin mask; grader VAS as reference
markers.norms: Units: SD of CIELAB channels (method-dependent). Norms: not found
markers.perception: More homogeneous skin colour judged younger, healthier and more attractive (Fink 2006; Matts 2007). Cross-cultural replication with Maasai and Tsimane' raters (Fink 2017). Colour distribution is linked more strongly to perceived health, surface topography to perceived age (Samson 2011). Skin colour uniformity was a main attribute in perceived age (Nkengne 2008)

markers.name: Facial redness (a\*) / erythema
markers.definition: Redness of facial skin from blood perfusion and oxygenation; diffuse or focal erythema
markers.photo: CCC, XPL strongly preferred (glare inflates the colour estimate)
markers.method: CIELAB a\* ROI mean; haemoglobin component map via ICA of skin colour (Tsumura 2003); focal erythema = area above a threshold
markers.norms: a\* units. Norms: not found
markers.perception: Raters raised skin blood colour (especially oxygenated) above baseline to make faces look healthier (Stephen 2009a). Facial skin colour affects perceived health (Stephen 2009b)

markers.name: Skin yellowness (b\*) / carotenoid colour
markers.definition: Yellowness of skin, partly from dietary carotenoids
markers.photo: CCC, XPL, no self-tanner or makeup
markers.method: CIELAB b\* ROI mean (melanin also raises b\*, so interpret alongside L\*/ITA)
markers.norms: b\* units. Norms: not found
markers.perception: Carotenoid-like yellowness raised apparent health more than melanin colour (Stephen 2011; review by Whitehead 2012). Framed mainly for light-skinned Asian and Caucasian faces (Whitehead 2012). Skin colour, not morphological masculinity, predicted male attractiveness (Scott 2010)

markers.name: Skin lightness / luminance (L\*)
markers.definition: Overall lightness of facial skin
markers.method: CIELAB L\* ROI mean
markers.norms: L\* (0–100). Norms: not found
markers.perception: L\* is part of the colour manipulations in Stephen 2011 (melanin axis). Skin luminance is the reference for facial contrast (Russell 2009)

markers.name: Brown / age spots (pigmented lesions)
markers.definition: Discrete hyperpigmented macules (solar lentigines, freckles, age spots)
markers.method: Spot segmentation on the L\* or melanin map: count, area %, contrast vs surrounding skin; atlas grading (Skin Aging Atlas pigmentation items)
markers.norms: Count / area %; Atlas grades (ordinal). Norms: not found
markers.perception: Pigmented age spots were heritable, roughly half genetic and half environmental (Gunn 2009). Brown spots drove younger graders' age estimates (Nkengne 2008). Pigmentation heterogeneity is one of four aging-sign categories (Flament 2013)

markers.name: Post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation (PIH)
markers.definition: Macular hyperpigmentation left after inflammatory lesions (mainly acne)
markers.method: Lesion segmentation and classification (Seité 2019 algorithm identified PIH); colour contrast vs normal skin; Taylor Hyperpigmentation Scale (skin-colour cards) for grading
markers.norms: Count/area; Taylor scale (visual card scale; details not accessed). Middle East: PIH in 87.2% of acne patients, lasting ≥1 year in 52.6%, more bothersome than acne for half (Abanmi 2019). Jeddah: PIH alone 22.3%, PIH + scarring 36.2% (Alamri 2025)
markers.perception: Burden and quality of life only; no attractiveness data found
markers.sources: Abanmi 2019; Alamri 2025; Davis & Callender 2010; Taylor 2002; Taylor 2005; Seité 2019

markers.name: Melasma-pattern pigmentation
markers.definition: Symmetric, ill-defined brown patches in centrofacial or malar pattern
markers.method: Reviewer MASI/mMASI (area × darkness [× homogeneity] by facial region). Pixel proxy: area and darkness of the hyperpigmented mask by region
markers.norms: MASI; modified MASI drops homogeneity with no loss of reliability (Pandya 2011). Score ranges: not checked in the original. Gulf prevalence: 2.9% in Hail (Parthasaradhi 1998), cited through a secondary review only and not confirmed
markers.perception: No perception data found. Differential diagnosis in Saudi women: pigmentary demarcation lines (Al-Samary 2010)

markers.name: Facial pigmentary demarcation lines (PDL)
markers.definition: Sharp physiological lines between darker and lighter facial skin (e.g. line F)
markers.method: Reviewer identification of line type; pixel edge contrast along the lateral face
markers.norms: Presence/type. 14% of 1,033 Saudi women screened (median onset age 16; line F most common at 53%) (Al-Samary 2010)
markers.perception: Not found

markers.name: Under-eye darkness (periorbital hyperpigmentation, "dark circles")
markers.definition: Darkening of the lower (and upper) eyelid skin compared with the cheek
markers.photo: CCC, XPL, frontal, eyes open, light from the front (overhead light adds shadow)
markers.method: ΔL\*, Δa\*, Δb\* (or ΔITA) between infraorbital ROI and cheek ROI. Subtype by colour: brownish = pigment, bluish/violaceous = vascular. Separate from shadow by also measuring hollowness
markers.norms: ΔL\* etc. Norms: not found. Singapore clinic subtypes: vascular 41.8%, constitutional 38.6%, PIH 12%, shadow 11.4% (Ranu 2011)
markers.perception: Dark circles drove younger graders' age estimates (Nkengne 2008). Reviewed as giving a tired or aged look (Sarkar 2016, abstract not read)

markers.name: Under-eye hollowness / tear trough
markers.definition: Depression of the infraorbital region (tear trough / infraorbital hollow)
markers.photo: Frontal + 45° obliques, controlled frontal lighting (shadow is the signal), neutral expression
markers.method: Allergan Infraorbital Hollows Scale (5-point photonumeric); Merz mid-face infraorbital hollow scale (5-point); Tear Trough Rating Scale. Pixel proxy: shading depth from luminance or 3D shape estimate
markers.norms: 5-point (0–4) ordinal. A ≥1-point difference is clinically significant; intrarater κ 0.79, interrater κ 0.70 (Donofrio 2016)
markers.perception: Shading in the eye area is part of the "eye area" age cue (Nkengne 2008)

markers.name: Horizontal forehead lines
markers.definition: Static (at rest) and dynamic (brow raise) horizontal forehead wrinkles
markers.photo: Frontal, hair off the forehead, raking or controlled light; rest + brow-raise images
markers.method: Allergan Forehead Lines Scale (5-point photonumeric, static); Merz upper-face forehead lines scale; automated line detection (Cula 2013)
markers.norms: 5-point (0–4). Allergan: ≥1-point difference is clinically significant (Carruthers 2016)
markers.perception: Wrinkling independently linked to looking old for one's age (Gunn 2009)

markers.name: Glabellar (frown) lines
markers.definition: Vertical lines between the brows
markers.method: 4-point 0–3 glabellar score (Honeck 2003); Merz 5-point glabellar scale (Flynn 2012)
markers.norms: 0–3: interobserver κ 0.62 (Honeck 2003). Merz: 0–4
markers.perception: General wrinkle–age link (Gunn 2009); no glabellar-specific perception data found

markers.name: Crow's feet (lateral canthal lines)
markers.definition: Lines radiating from the lateral canthus
markers.method: Validated 5-point crow's feet scale (Carruthers 2008a); Merz crow's feet at rest and dynamic (Flynn 2012); auto line detection
markers.norms: 0–4 ordinal
markers.perception: General wrinkle–age link (Gunn 2009); eye area was the main age-perception attribute (Nkengne 2008)

markers.name: Nasolabial fold severity
markers.definition: Depth and length of the nasolabial fold
markers.photo: Frontal + obliques, neutral expression, controlled light
markers.method: Wrinkle Severity Rating Scale (5-grade); Modified Fitzpatrick Wrinkle Scale; Merz nasolabial scale (Narins 2012); newer NLF photonumeric scale (Lorenc 2024)
markers.norms: WSRS 1–5. MFWS: intra-assessor κ 0.71 with photos only, 0.79 with photos + descriptions (Shoshani 2008)
markers.perception: Nasolabial fold drove younger graders' age estimates (Nkengne 2008)

markers.name: Marionette lines
markers.definition: Lines or folds running down from the oral commissures
markers.method: Marionette Lines Grading Scale (5-point photonumeric); Merz lower-face scales; newer 2024 photonumeric scale
markers.norms: 0–4 ordinal
markers.perception: Not found

markers.name: Global facial wrinkling (Fitzpatrick / Lemperle)
markers.definition: Overall wrinkle depth and extent, or per-site wrinkle class
markers.method: Fitzpatrick wrinkle classification (classes I–III with sub-scores); Lemperle 0–5 photo-referenced grade per wrinkle; automated orientation/frequency filtering tested against clinical 11-point scales (Cula 2013)
markers.norms: Lemperle 0–5: 92.7% identical live ratings, 87% correlation with profilometry depth (Lemperle 2001). Fitzpatrick class details: original not accessed
markers.perception: Skin wrinkling, hair greying and lip height were each independently linked to looking old for one's age (Gunn 2009)

markers.name: Global photoaging type (Glogau) / atlas photodamage
markers.definition: Overall photoageing category from wrinkles, pigmentation, texture
markers.method: Glogau types (reviewer); correlated with VISIA-CR measurements (Oesch 2022); Skin Aging Atlas grades; atrophic photodamage 9-point photonumeric scale (Ayer 2018)
markers.norms: Glogau type I–IV (definitions not checked in the original; abstract not available). Ayer: 0–8
markers.perception: Sun-exposure-related signs linked to age perception (Flament 2013; Gunn 2009)
markers.sources: Glogau 1996; Oesch 2022; Ayer 2018; Bazin & Doublet 2007; Flament 2013

markers.name: Pore visibility (size/density)
markers.definition: Visible enlarged pore openings, mainly cheeks and nose
markers.photo: Close-up cheek, controlled (ideally polarised) light, high resolution; phone selfies are borderline
markers.method: Pore detection: threshold diameter, count/cm², % surface covered (Flament 2015); Skin Aging Atlas pore grades
markers.norms: Detection threshold 250 µm; size mm², density N/cm², coverage %. Varies strongly by ethnicity; very low in Chinese women (Flament 2015). Pore size also measured by Perkins 2011
markers.perception: Self-declared "enlarged pores" followed the measurements (Flament 2015); no attractiveness data found

markers.name: Skin surface texture / roughness (topography)
markers.definition: Fine surface irregularities (micro-relief, unevenness) apart from discrete wrinkles
markers.photo: Close-up, raking or controlled light, no makeup
markers.method: High-frequency texture energy, Gabor/LBP features on luminance; topography removal experiments (Samson 2011)
markers.norms: Unitless image metrics; norms not found
markers.perception: Removing surface-topography cues had a stronger effect on perceived age than evening out colour (Samson 2011)

markers.name: Acne global severity (IGA / GAGS / GEA)
markers.definition: Overall acne severity grade
markers.photo: Frontal + both profiles, diffuse light; Seité used smartphone photos
markers.method: IGA (FDA: 5-point, qualitative, no lesion counts in the grade definitions); GAGS (regional factor × lesion grade 0–4); GEA scale; Hayashi classification; AI grading from smartphone photos (Seité 2019)
markers.norms: GAGS factors (secondary sources; original not accessed): forehead 2, each cheek 2, nose 1, chin 1, chest/back 3. Bands 1–18 mild, 19–30 moderate, 31–38 severe, ≥39 very severe. IGA 0 clear – 4 severe (FDA). GEA validated on photos (R = 0.8057) (Dréno 2011)
markers.perception: Psychosocial impact only; no attractiveness data in these sources
markers.sources: Doshi 1997; FDA 2018; Dréno 2011; Hayashi 2008; Seité 2019; Tan 2006

markers.name: Acne lesion counts (inflammatory / non-inflammatory)
markers.definition: Counts of comedones, papules, pustules, nodules
markers.photo: High-resolution frontal + profiles; close-ups for comedones
markers.method: Manual counting or AI detection (Seité 2019 identified comedonal vs inflammatory lesions and PIH)
markers.norms: Counts. Reliability of dermatologist counts studied by Tan 2006 (values not in abstract). Prevalence differs by ethnicity (Perkins 2011: 37% African American, 32% Hispanic, 23–30% other groups)
markers.perception: Not found

markers.name: Acne scarring
markers.definition: Atrophic (icepick, boxcar, rolling) and hypertrophic post-acne scars
markers.photo: Frontal + obliques with raking light (atrophic scars depend on shadow)
markers.method: Goodman & Baron qualitative global grade (4 grades); ECCA (6 items, weighted global score); scar detection from shading
markers.norms: Goodman grade 1–4; ECCA global score. Jeddah: scarring alone 22.8%, with PIH 36.2% (Alamri 2025)
markers.perception: Goodman grading uses how visible scars are at social distance (Goodman 2006); no formal perception study found

markers.name: Skin gloss / oiliness / shine
markers.definition: Specular reflection from the skin surface (sebum, sweat)
markers.photo: Controlled lighting essential; parallel- vs cross-polarised pair ideal; fixed exposure; record time since cleansing and ambient heat/humidity (relevant in the Gulf climate)
markers.method: Specular-highlight area and intensity (pixels above threshold; gradient between specular and diffuse) (Ezerskaia 2017); texture-statistics gloss model (Wang 2021); surface-reflection histogram SD and skewness (Matsubara 2012)
markers.norms: Gloss units relative to calibration standards; no validated photo scale or facial norms found
markers.perception: Perceived surface reflection explained by SD and skewness of the surface-reflection image (Matsubara 2012); no attractiveness/health data found

markers.name: Skin radiance / glow (subsurface brightness)
markers.definition: Perceived luminous quality of skin, mainly from subsurface reflection
markers.photo: Polarised pair or tightly controlled light; CCC
markers.method: Mean of the subsurface-reflection image histogram (Matsubara 2012)
markers.norms: Unitless; norms not found
markers.perception: Perceived subsurface reflection explained by the subsurface histogram mean (Matsubara 2012)

markers.name: Apparent skin health (cheek patch)
markers.definition: Rated healthiness of an isolated skin patch, a composite of colour and texture
markers.method: Observer ratings of cheek patches; can be used as a training target
markers.norms: Rating scale (study-specific)
markers.perception: Rated skin-patch health correlated with, and causally influenced, male facial attractiveness independent of shape (Jones 2004)

markers.name: Limbal ring visibility (presence/contrast)
markers.definition: Dark ring where the iris meets the sclera; how distinct and opaque it is
markers.photo: High-resolution eye crop, eyes wide open, gaze at lens, diffuse frontal light (catchlights and reflections spoil it), CCC for contrast
markers.method: Radial luminance profile across the iris–sclera border: contrast (ΔL\*) and sharpness. Reviewer 3-level grade (absent / faint / distinct)
markers.norms: Unitless contrast; norms not found. Ring prominence decreases with age (Peshek 2011, stated in abstract)
markers.perception: Faces with a dark, distinct limbal ring rated more attractive, also when inverted (Peshek 2011). Targets with limbal rings rated healthier; women preferred them in short-term mating contexts (Brown & Sacco 2018)

markers.name: Limbal ring width
markers.definition: Radial width of the dark annulus relative to iris radius
markers.photo: As above, at high resolution (iris ≥ ~100 px across)
markers.method: Width at half-maximum of the radial darkness profile ÷ iris radius
markers.norms: Ratio; norms not found. Width and opacity depend on iris pigmentation and the optics of the region (Peshek 2011; Shyu & Wyatt 2009)
markers.perception: Same as visibility; width was not tested separately in the abstracts

markers.name: Scleral redness
markers.definition: Redness of the visible sclera (vascular injection)
markers.photo: Eye crop, eyes wide open, CCC, diffuse light, no flash
markers.method: Segment sclera; mean a\*; optional vessel area %
markers.norms: a\*; norms not found. Male sclera redder than female (Kramer 2022)
markers.perception: Digitally reddened sclera rated less healthy, less attractive and older (Provine 2013a). Lower redness → younger, healthier, more attractive (Russell 2014). Redder/yellower sclera → more masculine (Kramer 2022)

markers.name: Scleral yellowness
markers.definition: Yellow tint of the sclera
markers.method: Sclera mask mean b\*
markers.norms: b\*; norms not found. Increases with age (Russell 2014; Kramer 2022)
markers.perception: Yellowed sclera rated less healthy, less attractive and older (Provine 2013a; Russell 2014)

markers.name: Scleral lightness ("whiteness")
markers.definition: Lightness of the sclera
markers.method: Sclera mask mean L\*
markers.norms: L\*; darker with age (Russell 2014)
markers.perception: "Super-white" sclera rated younger but not healthier or more attractive (Provine 2013a). Darker sclera → older (Russell 2014). Scleral colour was measured against eye-area attractiveness by Gründl 2012 (direction partly truncated in abstract)

markers.name: Binocular asymmetry of scleral redness
markers.definition: Difference in redness between left and right sclera
markers.method: Left–right difference in sclera a\*
markers.norms: Δa\*; norms not found
markers.perception: Studied as a cue to sadness, healthiness, attractiveness (Provine 2013b; abstract not retrieved, direction not verified)

markers.name: Iris colour
markers.definition: Iris hue and lightness (brown → blue/green)
markers.photo: Eye crop, CCC, diffuse light, no coloured contact lenses (ask)
markers.method: Iris mask CIELAB; categorical classification
markers.norms: Categorical / CIELAB. Gulf populations are predominantly dark-irised; no Gulf norms found
markers.perception: No correlation between iris colour and eye-area attractiveness (Gründl 2012). Brown-eyed male faces rated more trustworthy, but the effect came from associated face shape (Kleisner 2013). Eye colour was a factor in cross-cultural attractiveness ratings (Kočnar 2019)

markers.name: Under-eye bags (lower-eyelid fullness / fat prolapse)
markers.definition: Convex bulging of the lower eyelid
markers.photo: Frontal + profile/oblique, neutral gaze, controlled light
markers.method: Reviewer grade; 3D or shading convexity proxy. No validated photonumeric bag scale found. Tear-trough/IOH scales cover the concavity, not the bulge
markers.norms: Not found
markers.perception: Eye area was the leading attribute for perceived age (Nkengne 2008); bag-specific evidence not found

markers.name: Eye opening (palpebral fissure height)
markers.definition: Vertical opening of the eye at rest
markers.method: Landmark distance (upper–lower lid at mid-pupil) ÷ interpupillary distance
markers.norms: Ratio; norms not found (Farkas 2005 gives ethnic anthropometric norms for related eye measurements; full text not accessed)
markers.perception: "Eyes opening" drove older graders' age estimates (Nkengne 2008)

markers.name: Pupil diameter (relative)
markers.definition: Pupil size relative to iris
markers.photo: Eye crop; fixed ambient light (pupil size depends on light)
markers.method: Pupil/iris diameter ratio
markers.norms: Ratio; norms not found
markers.perception: Tested for eye-area attractiveness by Gründl 2012 (result in truncated part of abstract, not verified)

markers.name: Facial averageness (prototypicality)
markers.definition: How close a face's shape is to the population mean face
markers.photo: Frontal, neutral, no head tilt; landmarks visible (head covering can hide the hairline)
markers.method (how operationalised from 2d phot: Landmark shape distance (Procrustes) from a sex- and population-specific average; composites built by averaging (Langlois 1990); warping toward or away from an average (Rhodes 2001)
markers.norms: Procrustes distance (unitless). Needs a Gulf reference average (none published that we found)
markers.perception: Averaged composites rated more attractive (Langlois 1990). Meta-analytic review of attractiveness (Langlois 2000). Averageness raised attractiveness in Chinese and Japanese faces (Rhodes 2001a). Faces closer to average rated more attractive across 10 cultures incl. Turkey (Kočnar 2019). Averageness vs symmetry compared (Komori 2009a). Averageness/symmetry vs actual health (Rhodes 2001b)
markers.sources: Langlois 1990; Langlois 2000; Rhodes 2001a; Rhodes 2001b; Komori 2009a; Kočnar 2019

markers.name: Facial symmetry / fluctuating asymmetry (FA)
markers.definition: Bilateral asymmetry of paired landmarks; FA = random (non-directional) deviation
markers.photo: Strictly frontal, camera at eye level, neutral expression (head rotation creates fake asymmetry)
markers.method (how operationalised from 2d phot: Landmark-based: mirror-and-relabel Procrustes asymmetry, split into directional and fluctuating parts; midline-deviation indices; perfectly symmetric versions made by blending a face with its mirror image (Rhodes 2001a)
markers.norms: Unitless. Norms: not found
markers.perception: Symmetric versions preferred (Rhodes 2001a). Measured symmetry linked to attractiveness, but via correlated cues such as masculinity; raters could not judge symmetry accurately (Scheib 1999). Symmetry and averageness (Grammer 1994). Preferences for symmetry vs developmental instability (Simmons 2004). FA had no effect on cross-cultural attractiveness (Kočnar 2019)
markers.sources: Grammer 1994; Scheib 1999; Rhodes 2001a; Simmons 2004; Penton-Voak 2001; Kočnar 2019

markers.name: Sexual shape dimorphism (morphometric masculinity–femininity index)
markers.definition: Where a face's shape lies on the male–female shape axis
markers.method (how operationalised from 2d phot: Geometric morphometrics: discriminant function or projection onto the male–female mean vector (Scott 2010 classified >96% correctly). Population-specific; Kleisner 2021 showed dimorphism varies across populations
markers.norms: Unitless score; population-specific reference needed
markers.perception: Morphological masculinity did not predict male attractiveness; skin colour did (Scott 2010). Feminised faces preferred, including feminised male faces (Perrett 1998). Size of dimorphism varies across populations; dimorphism moderately linked to attractiveness in women, weakly or not in men (Kleisner 2021). Femininity linked to attractiveness across cultures (Kočnar 2019)

markers.name: Perceived masculinity (rated)
markers.definition: Observer-rated masculinity, mainly for male faces
